translations.text: And who knows whether he will be wise or foolish? Yet he will have control over all the work I have done and used my wisdom to accomplish under the sun. This too is futility.
And I praised the dead, who have already died, more than the living, who are still alive.
Do not let your mouth cause your body to sin, and do not say before God, “It was a mistake,” lest God become angry at your words and destroy the work of your hands.
Also, everyone to whom the Lord has given wealth and possessions, and whom he has enabled to eat from them, to receive his share, and to rejoice in his work—this too is a gift from God.
For the shelter of wisdom is like the shelter of money, but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to its possessor.
Do not be excessively righteous, and do not be overly wise, lest you become bewildered.
Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your strength, because there is no work, thought, knowledge, or wisdom in Sheol, where you are going.

Again I saw under the sun that the race does not belong to the swift, nor the battle to the mighty, nor bread to the wise, nor wealth to those with understanding, nor praise to the knowledgeable, because time and chance happen to them all.
Even when a fool walks along the road, he lacks sense, and everything he thinks is foolishness.
Send your bread out over the surface of the water, because after many days you will find it.
If the clouds are full of rain, they pour it out on the earth. And if a tree falls to the south or to the north, wherever the tree falls, there it will remain.

Rejoice, young man, in the days of your youth, and let them be pleasant for you. Walk in the ways of your heart and according to what your eyes see, but know that for all these things the Lord will bring you to judgment.
On the day when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men totter, and the women grinding cease because they are few, and the women looking through the windows grow dim.
